title: Struck or striking, I am done for
odia:
ଗାଈ ମାଇଲେ ମଲି
ଗାଈକି ମାଇଲେ ମଲି।
literal_meaning: If the cow strikes me, I am done for; if I strike the cow, I am done for.
meaning_odia: ଗାଈ ମୋତେ ମାରିଲେ ବିପଦ, ମୁଁ ଗାଈକୁ ମାରିଲେ ମଧ୍ୟ ବିପଦ—ଦୁଇ ପଟୁ ଅଡ଼ୁଆର ଛବି। ଉତ୍ସର ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ଏହାକୁ ଦୋସନ୍ଧିରେ ପଡ଼ି କଣ କରିବା ଉଚିତ ନିର୍ଣ୍ଣୟ କରି ନପାରିବା ସହ ଯୋଡ଼େ।
explanation: The cow first does the striking, then receives it, but the speaker’s predicament remains unchanged. The inspected gloss identifies a dilemma in which deciding what to do becomes difficult. The repeated “I am done for” makes both alternatives feel closed off.
usage_example: Original imagined example: A coordinator faces two incompatible requests; accepting either will disappoint the other group. The saying expresses feeling trapped between the alternatives.
cultural_context: Adding କି changes the cow from the doer of the action to its object. That tiny grammatical shift reverses who strikes whom, while ମଲି remains the same at each line’s end. The force of the saying lies in the speaker being in trouble under both arrangements.

witnesses.locator: Page14, fifth item beginning ଗାଈ ମାଇଲେ.
witnesses.note: Rendered upload inspected17November2026; clear wording retained without repair. ମଲି is rendered idiomatically as I am done for, retaining the literal death-expression’s force.
Corresponding wording uses ଗୋରୁ / ଗୋରୁକୁ rather than uploaded ଗାଈ / ଗାଈକି. Explicit dilemma gloss; no claim of exact uploaded spelling or a prescribed punishment.

origin_note: Uploaded wording has a public counterpart with a different cattle term and object suffix. Earliest origin and shared lineage unknown.

odia_summary: ଯାହା କଲେ ମଧ୍ୟ ବିପଦ ଦେଖି ଦୋସନ୍ଧିରେ ପଡ଼ିବା।
english_summary: A dilemma in which either alternative leaves the speaker in trouble.
